title: Flow Escort: latency hedger and kernel gating for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce 95/99th tail latency during continuous prefill/decodes by introducing a lightweight admission layer (Flow Escort), speculative decode hedging, and a kernel-gating cost estimator to avoid harmful kernel switches under transient load.
background: We observe intermittent 95/99p latency spikes when mixed short and long sequences co-exist on a GPU. Current admission and batch-shaping decisions are reactive and sometimes trigger kernel switches that amplify tail latency. Past tickets improved batch shaping but we still see ~40-80ms spikes on heavy microbursts; customers with strict latency SLOs (e.g., realtime agents) are impacted.
proposed_solution: Implement 'Flow Escort' admission controller that performs: (1) sub-millisecond micro-profiling of incoming requests to assign them a lightweight flow tag (short/medium/long/elastic), (2) a kernel-gating estimator that scores the cost delta of switching kernels given the current batch mix, and (3) a speculative decode hedger that temporarily reserves micro-slots for likely tail requests to start speculative KV prewarm and early kernel prime. Admission will bias towards preserving kernel affinity when cost delta > threshold, while hedging reduces tail latency by starting speculative decodes for ~5% of requests identified as high-tail-risk. Include metrics, feature flags, and a canary rollout through runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: 95th latency for mixed short/long workload reduced >= 25% vs baseline (baseline measured on 2026-02-01)
99th latency reduced >= 15% for target workloads used in perf lab
No regression (>3%) in average token throughput for steady-state workloads
Feature toggles exist for: flow-escort admission, kernel-gating, speculative-hedging; defaults off for existing customers
End-to-end integration tests + stress test harness run in CI with synthetic microburst scenarios
Canary rollout plan with automatic rollback if 99p latency increases or error-rate > 0.5%

progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting — aligned on success metrics (95p and 99p targets) and canary constraints. Decided to implement cost-estimator in native runtime to minimize RPC overhead.

2026-02-24: Micro-profiling spec completed. Chosen features: incoming sequence length, user-supplied latency hint header, recent client token-rate (sliding window 500ms). Added synthetic probe plan to avoid extra CPU in steady-state.
2026-03-02: Prototype kernel-gating estimator implemented in feature branch. Early lab results show kernel-switch rate down 35% on mixed workload when estimator threshold tuned conservatively.

2026-03-06: Speculative hedger design reviewed by runtime team. Trade-off: hedging reduces tail but costs ~2-4% extra tokens served. Decided to default hedging to 0% and enable 5% in canary for latency-sensitive customers.
2026-03-10: Telemetry schema approved. New metrics: flow_tag, kernel_affinity_score, estimated_switch_cost, hedged_request=true/false. Added tracing hooks for kernel selection path.
2026-03-12: Integration tests green on internal CI. Preparing canary PR and rollout docs; open questions on backpressure interactions for Dedicated customers (TBC with infra)
tradeoffs_and_notes: Speculative hedging increases token compute by a small percent; acceptable for customers willing to trade cost for lower tail latency.
Kernel-gating relies on a compact cost model — has edge cases when models change topology; plan to invalidate micro-profiles on model/version change.
Flow tags are best-effort signals; will not be used to deny service. They inform admission prioritization and hedging decisions only.
Must ensure hedger and admission respect per-tenant quotas and Dedicated isolation constraints. Introduced tenant-level hedging caps.
Security: no PII shipped in telemetry. Telemetry review requested (see links).
metrics_baseline_and_targets: Baseline (mixed short/long synthetic): 95p=240ms, 99p=380ms, avg throughput 1100 tokens/s per GPU
Kernel-switch rate target: reduce harmful switches by >=30% in microburst windows
